content:
maya: heads up — i'm about to push a refactor called 'slab-tilt rebalancer' that shifts small batches between slabs to reduce burst-induced starvation. quick summary: detect skewed occupancy, gently nudge a few requests across slab boundaries per epoch.
jon: curious how this fits with the existing admission interface. is this an adapter or a scheduler-side change?
kevin: scheduler-side. the idea is a standalone rebalancer loop that talks to the queue manager via the existing lease API. it only takes "soft" takeovers (won't preempt in-flight token batches) and emits a small handshake event so downstream operators can adjust.
sara: metrics/telemetry concerns — this could hide/skew headroom signals. how do we keep observability sliceable by tenant?
maya: plan: feature flag + shadow mode first. export tilt_shifts_total, tilt_shift_latency_ms, slab_starvation_rate, and per-tenant shift_counts. also add a tag to shifted requests so eval pipeline can filter.
jon: edge cases: kv-cache thrash and seqid reordering — any safeguards?
kevin: yes, two main guards: 1) only shift requests whose kv-cache affinity is absent (cold requests) OR whose sequence preserves prefix ordering; 2) max_shift_per_epoch cap to avoid mass moves. pseudo-config:

```
slab_tilt {
  enabled: true
  epoch_ms: 200
  max_shift_per_epoch: 4
  soft_takeover: true
  tag_shifted_requests: "slab_tilt.v1"
}
```

maya: rollout steps: shadow->10%->50%->100% over ~2w, with automatic rollback if slab_starvation_rate increases >2x or p99 latency regresses >10% for 5m.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: release 'slab-tilt/v0.1' created by @kevin. CI passed. Use releasesctl to rollout.
jon: what's the migration contract for adapters that assumed slab affinity? some adapters bind to slab ids for locality.
kevin: we provide a stable slab id in the request header and a "shifted_from" meta when we move it. adapters that need strict locality should opt-out via allow_tilt=false in route config. default preserve backwards compatibility.
sara: can we simulate cross-slab KV cache hits in canary? would like a replay mode to inject shifted tags into shadow traces.
maya: yes — adding a replay mode in the QA harness, will push scripts to perf infra. example rollout command:

```
releasesctl rollout --service slab-tilt --percent 10 --timeout 30m
```

kevin: i'll open the PR with the rebalancer and the telemetry dashboards. PR: github.com/redwood/retenge/pull/1234
maya: great. please add a short FAQ in the PR about when to opt-out per-route and the expected perf delta (usually reduces p50 by ~15-25% on bursty traces).
jon: thanks — i'll review the API surface for the lease handshake.
sara: I'll coordinate canary runs once PR lands. :thumbsup:
kevin: note — fallback: deterministic round-robin rebalancer if telemetry shows heap churn; kill-switch is `slab_tilt.enabled=false`.
maya: sounds good. landing this afternoon in shadow mode. ping me if you see any immediate oddities.
